pre_reflection.text:
[Pre-reflection] The strategy's reliance on rigid entry filters (RSI > 50 + Bollinger crossover) may cause frequent whipsaws in ranging markets, while the ATR filter's threshold of 0.001 is arbitrary and may not scale well across assets. The exit logic is too simplistic, relying on RSI levels that can lead to premature exits during strong trends. Overfitting risk is high due to the lack of out-of-sample validation and sensitivity to small parameter changes.
[Backup plan] If results are poor, switch to a momentum-based entry (e.g., 14-period RSI above 50 with 5-period momentum confirmation) and implement a trailing stop instead of fixed Bollinger exits. If Sharpe is mediocre, adjust ATR threshold to 0.002 and test dynamic RSI thresholds (e.g., 40-70 range). As a fallback, try a mean-reversion approach using Bollinger bands alone with volatility-adjusted position sizing and trend filter (e.g., 50-period EMA).

iterations.hypothesis: Combining ADX trend filter with RSI and Bollinger Bands creates a robust entry system that avoids trading against the trend while using volatility-based stops to manage risk effectively.
